problem: ObjectNav agents see only a small, occluded part of an unseen house, so they must guess where the target object is. Prior methods either map only what has been observed (GOSE/SemExp top-down maps) or learn priors implicitly or from language/video (SAVN, scene-graph methods, VLV). None of them explicitly predicts the unobserved scene with calibrated uncertainty for the planner to use.
motivation: Finding an object category in an unknown house depends on functional and spatial priors about indoor layouts, e.g. beds are in bedrooms and nightstands sit beside beds. Semantic scene completion can encode such priors directly as a predicted map, but its predictions are noisy. A navigation policy therefore needs to know how far to trust each predicted region. The key observation is that completion alone does not help navigation unless it comes with a self-supervised confidence estimate.
key_idea: Complete the agent-centric semantic top-down map beyond the field of view with a scene completion network, predict a per-pixel self-supervised confidence map for that completion, and feed both into a DQN that acts through a dense spatial action map.
insight: Explicit scene completion only pays off when it comes with learned confidence. Adding completion without confidence (SSCNav-F 21.7/11.7 SR/SPL) is no better than no completion (SSCNav-CF 21.8/11.8), while adding the confidence map gives 27.1/15.7 (+5.3 SR, +3.9 SPL). A learned confidence also beats a binary seen/unseen mask (SSCNav/BC 25.2/15.0), so it carries more than visibility information. The gains are largest for objects with strong contextual bias (toilet, shower, sink) and smallest for ubiquitous objects (sofa, table). The dense spatial action map matters a lot: replacing it with 8 discrete turn-then-move actions drops SR to 10.9. The trend holds with ground-truth segmentation (G+SSCNav 43.8/25.9 vs G+SSCNav-CF 38.7/23.2).
method: Semantic observation map: ACNet segments each 480x640 RGB-D frame (40 MP3D categories); the last 5 frames are fused into a point cloud using GT poses, height-filtered to between floor and 1.55 m, and projected into a 6m x 6m agent-centric, orientation-aligned one-hot (N+1 channel) semantic top-down map o_t.

Semantic scene completion network: a fully convolutional ResNet-style net (1 max-pool, 4 down-sample and 5 up-sample residual blocks) predicts semantic labels for unobserved cells. It is trained with pixel-wise cross-entropy on regions unobserved in the input but observed in the target map. Training data are 52,300 GT maps from random exploration, each paired with 4 inputs built by randomly dropping views (1-4 views kept).

Self-calibrated confidence network: a second branch with the same architecture takes o_t and the completed map ô_t. It regresses a per-pixel correctness map in [0,1], supervised by whether the completion matches ground truth, with MSE on unobserved regions only.

Spatial-action-map DQN policy: the state is the completed map, the confidence map and a tiled one-hot target category, concatenated. A fully convolutional double-DQN outputs a Q-value per pixel; the agent turns toward the argmax pixel and moves forward up to 0.25 m. Rewards are -0.01 per step, -0.25 for moving less than 0.125 m, a delta-geodesic-distance-to-closest-target term, and +10 on success.

Stop checker: the camera is rotated 4 times about the z-axis. The episode stops if more than 5,000 target-category pixels lie within 1 m in any view, or after 500 steps. Success requires the stop decision, being within 1 m of a target instance, and the target being visible.

setting.backbone: ACNet RGB-D segmentation + ResNet-style FCN completion and confidence networks + FCN double-DQN policy (all trained, no large pretrained model)
setting.training_data: ACNet trained on 209,200 RGB-D images (40 categories) from MP3D training houses; completion and confidence nets trained on 52,300 GT top-down maps (x4 randomly view-dropped inputs) from random exploration of MP3D train houses; policy trained with RL in Habitat on MP3D train houses with episodes of uniformly sampled target categories
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (480x640, camera 1.25 m high, tilted -30°) + GT pose sensor
setting.action_space: dense spatial action map over a 6m x 6m agent-centric top-down map: pick a pixel, turn toward it, move forward up to 0.25 m; stop decided by a heuristic stop checker
setting.privileged: GT camera pose (as in the Habitat 2020 ObjectNav setting); stop checker takes 4 extra rotated views; G+ variants use GT semantic segmentation of observations

numbers_note: Scene completion IoU (715 samples from unseen houses) appears only as a bar plot (Fig. 5), with no numeric values. Table I also gives per-category SR/SPL, not transcribed here. Other ablation averages: SSCNav-F 0.217/0.117, SSCNav/BC 0.252/0.150, G+SSCNav-F 0.357/0.235, G+SSCNav-CF 0.387/0.232; SAVN baseline 0.009/0.009. The text claims SSCNav/SA drops SPL by 14.8%, but Table I implies 11.2 (0.157 vs 0.045). The split is not named; the 687 episodes are 'from unseen houses in Matterport3D provided by Habitat', so the val subset is assumed. The protocol (7 categories, custom actions and stop checker) is not comparable to standard MP3D ObjectNav leaderboards.
results: On 687 unseen-house MP3D episodes over 7 categories, SSCNav reaches 27.1% SR / 15.7 SPL. This beats the authors' GOSE-style re-implementation without completion (21.8/11.8) and fine-tuned SAVN (0.9/0.9). With GT segmentation it reaches 43.8/25.9, versus 38.7/23.2 without completion. Learned confidence beats binary visibility confidence by +1.9 SR / +0.7 SPL, and the spatial action map beats sparse actions by +16.2 SR.
limitations: Non-standard evaluation (7 categories, 687 episodes, custom success rule with visibility, 4-view stop checker, custom action space), so results are not comparable to standard Habitat ObjectNav numbers. The GOSE comparison is only the authors' own re-implementation.
Depends on GT pose and strongly on segmentation quality (27.1 vs 43.8 SR with GT segmentation). Absolute success is low, and completion without confidence gives no benefit.

The policy sees only a local 6m x 6m map built from the last 5 frames, with no long-term global memory, which likely hurts large-house exploration. Gains are small for objects without strong contextual bias (sofa, table).
